facts.text: Stanley was renamed in 1957 to honor 'Uncle Jack Stanley,' a local benefactor who helped orphan boys.
The area began as an unincorporated community called Oak Grove in the late 19th century, settled by farmers and preachers who taught in pine log cabins.
Stanley High School, originally Oak Grove High School, expanded in the 1950s with a new brick grade school, lunchroom, and football stadium, aided by federal vocational programs.
The first diploma graduates of the local school were Hazel Bowden and Lewis Hayden Christian in 1921, after years of short terms and basic facilities.
Olivet Baptist Church, founded around 1889, and local Methodist congregations shared early facilities with schools, shaping community consolidation.
